title: Checkpoint duplicated when a session-end hook is killed between the v1 write and the state save

verdict.rationale: The condense-inside-callback structure came from the lock-funnelling refactor, which was about serialising state writes and never considered a kill between the v1 write and the state save. The later commit (53644bedea) acknowledges the window but only as a known, unfixed limitation, deferred as a follow-up, so it was not a choice of the duplicate-checkpoint behaviour.

evidence.text:
Funnel all session-state mutations through MutateSessionState

The previous PostToolUse-only lock fixed parallel PostToolUse races but
left every other writer (TurnEnd, PostCommit, condense, model update,
review env adoption, attribution divergence, post-rewrite remap, etc.)
doing its own unlocked load → mutate → save. A PostToolUse save could
still revert Phase, CheckpointTranscriptStart, TurnCheckpointIDs, token
usage, and other fields if it landed between another writer's load and
save.

Convert every session-state load-modify-save in the lifecycle dispatcher
and strategy package to MutateSessionState (or, for the rare new-state
case, to wrap the lone save in acquireSessionGate). The helper now:
  - Takes an OS flock against .git/entire-session-locks/<id>.lock for
    the duration of the load + fn + save.
  - Layers a per-process gate keyed by goroutine ID over the flock so
    nested calls in the same goroutine share the outer's state pointer
    rather than deadlocking on a second flock or losing inner updates
    to the outer save.
  - Returns ErrStateNotFound when no state file exists, letting callers
    distinguish "no session" from a successful no-op.
  - Honours ErrMutationSkip so fn can decline to save when the merge
    produced no change (key for the PostToolUse hot path).

Lock files moved out of .git/entire-sessions/ so callers that enumerate
session state (tests, doctor, status) don't have to filter them.
ClearSessionState sweeps the lock too.

Address ULID review: display, fetch-hint, docs, id-const, lazy mint

Follow-ups from review of the git-refs ULID-emission PR (the id-kind read-routing
item, #1, and the write-boundary kind guard, #2, are deferred — see below):

- id.CheckpointID.DisplayShort() (new): kind-aware trim — legacy hex shows its
  12-char prefix, a ULID is shown in full (front-truncating a ULID drops its
  entropy tail and yields an ambiguous, unresolvable prefix).
- explain checkpoint-list view uses DisplayShort instead of a blind 12-char cut,
  so ULID checkpoints no longer collapse to near-identical timestamp prefixes.
- blame --long sizes the Checkpoint/Session column to its content
  (attributionCheckpointColumnWidth) so a 26-char ULID + session renders whole
  instead of being clipped to a session-less 21-char prefix.
- attach's fetch hint now resolves its target via resolveCheckpointFetchTarget —
  the same path FetchCheckpointRef uses — so the pasteable command matches the
  remote the fetch actually ran (fixes a bare "git fetch origin …" that fails in
  a token-only environment with an SSH origin).
- id.MaxIDLength ties to oklog/ulid's EncodedSize instead of a third hardcoded 26.
- eager-condense mints the checkpoint ID only after the skip checks, so a no-op
  session stop no longer pays the mint (and its checkpoints-config load).
- docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md: checkpoint IDs are 12-hex OR
  ULID (not fixed-width), minted via checkpoint.GenerateCheckpointID.

Serialize parallel PostToolUse writes with a per-session file lock

Codex parallelizes tool calls, so multiple PostToolUse hook processes
can race the load → merge → save sequence in RecordFilesTouched. Without
serialization, two parallel apply_patch calls can lose each other's
FilesTouched merges (last writer wins on the whole state blob).

Wrap the critical section with an OS-level advisory lock against
.git/entire-sessions/<id>.lock — POSIX flock on Unix,
LockFileEx on Windows. Use a sibling .lock file rather than locking
the state file itself, since Save's atomic-rename pattern unlinks the
inode the flock would be held on. The .lock filename matches the
existing Clear() glob so cleanup paths still purge it.

Scope is intentionally narrow: only RecordFilesTouched participates in
the lock today. PostToolUse-vs-{TurnEnd,PostCommit} cross-handler races
remain (a stale RecordFilesTouched save can still revert fields those
handlers updated between our load and save), but the window is now
bounded by the load+save inside the lock rather than the full hook
subprocess duration. Full coverage will require converting all
session-state mutators to a shared MutateSessionState(ctx, fn) helper
— left as a follow-up.
